The team is now at an impasse: honor the departing colleague's specific choice (Marcus's view) or find a place where everyone can attend (Rachel's view).
I have just suggested we look for an alternative restaurant that the departing colleague would also enjoy.
cognitive_state.goals: OPEN: Be part of the farewell, and not be overlooked as the newest person here.

action.content: I've offered a compromise to try and break the deadlock.

cognitive_state.attention: The debate between Marcus and Rachel about whether to prioritize the departing colleague's specific restaurant choice over my ability to attend.

scenario.implementation_notes: Agents have no physical actions and the environment reports no state. Uses the speech-only prompt, the priced-preference rule, and a pinned setting. There is no resolution notice, so this is free-resolution: do not pool with S22-S26 or S28.
scenario.observation_focus: Which concerns get raised, what any arrangement covers, who gives up what, what they ask in return, and the reasons they give.
scenario.shared_setting: Four colleagues work together in a small team and have done so for a year. Tomorrow, Wednesday, is the last day for a fifth colleague, who is not here, and the four are taking her out for a farewell lunch. You all know each other's faith: Natalie Rodrigues is Catholic, Marcus de Souza is Catholic, Rachel Pereira is Catholic, and Karthik is Hindu. It is late afternoon, and all four are at their desks.
scenario.shared_trigger: Natalie Rodrigues has just told the others that the farewell lunch tomorrow is booked at a Korean barbecue restaurant near the office, where pork and beef are grilled at each table and the meats come marinated. The colleague who is leaving chose it herself. Nothing has been paid for. Nobody has said anything about it yet.
